questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The universities available and the course selection is very important. I would want the university to have an attractive location, be located in an interesting city, and for the universities to offer interesting courses in English. 

For me personally, I choose the location due to personal reasons, as my boyfriend was living in the same city/country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The whole process went very smoothly. I'd already lived in the city before, so that made it easier when arriving.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't think I would say that I received any assistance. I was put into contact with another student from the university in case I needed help, which I fortunately didn't.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms, both single and double.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no meal plan options, and only one kitchen for the whole dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The housing is cheap considering other options, it gives you a chance to meet other exchange students, it has a gym (very limited, but at least free) and washing machines that are very cheap. 

I enjoyed living on campus, close to school and in a very central area.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's first come, first serve. You have to be incredibly quick when they open for registrations. Everything will be taken within seconds/minutes if it's popular. However, you have a trial period where you can drop or add classes afterwards.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't remember as I didn't seek any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I tried to register for. I was only limited by overlapping schedules.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check the class schedule to be sure that the combination of classes you want don't overlap. And have backups ready in case all the spots are taken.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels were very chill, and most classes consisted of only lectures.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My biology classes were solely lectures. And very short classes compared to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Ceramics, Beginner Korean, Animal Behaviour and Sensory and Perception.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Ceramics was very chill and an easy A. Animal behavior was interesting and also very chill. 

Korean language class was intense but interesting and relevant.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay a korean insurance once I got my ARC.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: As I had been there before, the expenses were as expected. Food and transport is cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were exchange clubs, but students couldn't join other clubs. There were a few events for exchange students but most had a limited amount of spots and were first come, first serve.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't have any recommendations

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to other cities

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Easy as I had lived there before. 
It can be a bit difficult with the language barrier, but possible to get by.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and courses with group work. Join language exchange meet ups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier and there view on foreginers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: food

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
To make sure to explore other parts of the country.

To explore the city and have fun with friends, and to not worry about exams and grades.

To not over pack as you would want to bring a lot of new stuff home

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare insurance documents in English that states the total coverage amount. You can try and get out of paying the korean insurance by providing this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet new people and explore a different culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to show up for every class as attendance is mandatory.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
